title: Guided onboarding: detect first streaming session + validate checklist step (handle disconnect edge cases)
author: Hannah Rivera
description: Context: As part of the guided onboarding checklist, we want a reliable, privacy-safe way to automatically mark the “Try streaming responses” step complete once a project has successfully established a streaming session. This PR implements streaming-session detection from gateway/server signals and wires it into the checklist validation pipeline. Motivation: Support tickets and beta feedback show users frequently attempt streaming, hit disconnects/timeouts, and end up unsure whether they “did it right.” We need a validator that (a) only credits a true successful streaming start, (b) is robust to retries/reconnects, and (c) avoids counting request attempts that never yielded a streamed chunk/token. What’s in this PR: (1) New derived signal: first_streaming_session_at per (org_id, project_id). Computed from inference request lifecycle events (no prompt/response content). (2) Checklist validation: onboarding step `STREAMING_SESSION` is marked complete when we observe `stream_first_chunk_received` (or first_token) for any request in the project using a valid API key. Disconnects before first chunk do not complete the step. Disconnects after first chunk do complete the step (streaming was established) and are recorded with a close_reason for debugging. (3) Edge-case handling: - Client disconnect immediately after headers (SSE opened but no chunk): NOT counted. - Server-side 5xx after stream opened but before chunk: NOT counted. - Retries/reconnects with same request_id: deduped (idempotent updates). - Multiple concurrent streams: we take min(first_chunk_at). - Event arrival lag/out-of-order: validator tolerates up to 15 minutes of reordering by using event timestamps and a small reconciliation window. (4) API surface: checklist state endpoint now includes `validation_debug.streaming_session` for internal/admin use (gated by existing `X-Redwood-Admin`), to help Support troubleshoot why a step isn’t completing. (5) Tests: unit tests for the stream classifier + integration test using synthetic event sequences (normal completion, early disconnect, reconnect, out-of-order). Notes / privacy: This validator only uses request_id, org/project ids, model id, transport=streaming, timestamps, and stream close reason. It does not store or inspect prompt content or generated tokens. Related: - PR #48255 adds event emission + allowlist; this PR assumes `inference.stream.opened`, `inference.stream.first_chunk`, `inference.stream.closed` are being sent (with allowlisted properties). - ENG-23113 (first successful request) landed earlier; pattern is similar but uses streaming-specific signals. Rollout: This only affects the feature-flagged checklist. The derived signal is computed for all orgs but only read when the onboarding checklist is enabled. Backfill is intentionally not included; we start tracking from deploy forward (consistent with beta cohort).
commits: console-backend: add streaming session derived signal model + storage
gateway-events: add first_chunk + closed reason mapping into telemetry envelope
onboarding: implement STREAMING_SESSION validator + reconciliation window
tests: add synthetic event sequences for disconnect/retry/out-of-order cases
admin: expose streaming validation debug payload (gated)
conversation: Dylan Brooks: Can you clarify the definition of “successful streaming session” we’re using for the checklist? We should avoid counting a connection that opens and immediately drops before any data is streamed.

Hannah Rivera (author): Yup — step completes only on `inference.stream.first_chunk` (or first_token) for the project. `stream.opened` alone is not sufficient. Added tests for “opened then client_disconnect before first_chunk” to ensure it doesn’t credit.
Amara Diallo: Where do we get `close_reason` from? Please confirm we’re not leaking anything user-provided and that we only keep enum-ish values.

Hannah Rivera (author): Close reason comes from gateway classification (client_disconnect, upstream_timeout, upstream_error, normal_end). No headers, no body, no IP. It’s a small enum and is allowlisted in `property_allowlist.ts`.
Nadia Rahman: Out-of-order events are common in some regions during load. The 15m window seems reasonable, but can we make sure we don’t flap the checklist state if a late event arrives?

Hannah Rivera (author): The state write is monotonic: once `first_streaming_session_at` is set it never moves forward, and checklist step completion is also monotonic. Late events can only set the timestamp earlier (min) before completion, but once completed we do not recompute the step back to incomplete.
Chloe Martin: Please gate `validation_debug` behind admin only and make sure it’s not returned to normal users. Also: add a migration note for the new table/columns.

Hannah Rivera (author): Done — debug payload requires `X-Redwood-Admin` and is omitted otherwise. Added migration in `onboarding_signals` with a brief comment in the runbook section of the PR description.
Leila Farouk: For integration tests, can we include the reconnect scenario with same request_id to assert dedupe/idempotency?
Hannah Rivera (author): Added `reconnect_same_request_id_is_deduped` to the integration test suite and verified it passes locally + in CI.
Dylan Brooks: Approved once CI is green.

Hannah Rivera (author): Fixed export in `packages/telemetry/src/events/inference.ts`; reran CI.
